summary: Approved. The deliverable is the strongest form this ticket could take inside a docs-only repository: a 1005-line page that states plainly that reactory-azure is an example-only MIT reference rather than a commercial integration, reconciles the stale `commercial` registry value with file:line evidence and the exact out-of-repo fix, and then uses the module as a ten-step build walkthrough in which every step points at a real file and line. I re-derived the load-bearing technical claims from the server checkout rather than trusting the page or the agent-authored verifier: FQN and module fields, the eight-declared/nine-implemented interface mismatch and its TS2353/TS2339 consequence, the unimported Client/ResponseType and undeclared Graph packages, sendEmail's caught error plus the truthy Express return, getEmails' factory-before-try ordering, the commented-out storage scaffold and unused AnonymousCredential, the empty services/workflows arrays, the three `commercial` registry values, and core's two direct imports. All verified. The azure verifier passes 34/34 with 105 citations resolving, the reactor verifier passes 11/11 as invoked, and the single docs failure reproduces identically on origin/master, so it is not introduced here. All three acceptance criteria are met at documentation level; the only remaining item is the server-side licence correction, which cannot be made in this worktree and is correctly routed to a follow-up. Residual issues are non-blocking: the report's diffstat omits the two committed .ai-agent artefacts (so its '6 files' claim is stale), the introduction miscounts the renumbered sections, a few comparison citations are loose, and the reactor verifier's citation check is skipped when invoked as reported.
